objectives.text: Explain what bone mineral density measures and how it is assessed.
Name calcium's functions and the three hormones controlling blood calcium.
Separate modifiable from non-modifiable osteoporosis risk factors.
Explain why B vitamins matter to metabolism without supplying energy.
Describe iron-deficiency anaemia and its main causes worldwide.

terms.gloss: A measure of calcified bone tissue; it correlates with bone strength.
The clinical scan used to assess bone mineral density.
One of three hormones — with calcitriol and calcitonin — that hold blood calcium steady.
Bone loss severe enough to raise fracture risk. Described as a childhood disease with old-age consequences.
A non-protein helper a vitamin becomes, letting an enzyme do its work. It supplies no energy itself.
Too little iron to make enough functional haemoglobin, so less oxygen is carried.

questions.prompt: Blood calcium is held steady by which three hormones?
questions.why: Blood calcium is regulated tightly because it is needed for nerve and muscle function, not only for bone.
distractorNotes: Those govern blood glucose and stress.
Each affects bone, but they are not the three regulators.
Those act on circulation and digestion.

questions.prompt: If dietary calcium runs short, the body will:
options: Draw calcium out of the bone
Stop using calcium in the nerves
Excrete less of every other mineral
questions.why: Blood calcium is defended first because it is immediately vital. The skeleton is the reserve it is defended from.
distractorNotes: Nerve function is precisely what is being protected.
Not the mechanism.
Calcium is not absorbed that way.

questions.prompt: Which is a MODIFIABLE risk factor for osteoporosis?
options: Being female rather than being male
Being over the age of fifty
questions.why: Separating what can be changed from what cannot is the point: smoking, alcohol, inactivity and diet are all open to action.
distractorNotes: Non-modifiable.
Non-modifiable.
Non-modifiable.

questions.prompt: Osteoporosis is called a childhood disease with old-age consequences because:
options: Peak bone mass is built when young
Children are diagnosed with it most often
It is inherited directly from a parent
questions.why: Most bone is laid down early in life. How much was built then sets how much can be lost later before fracture risk rises.
distractorNotes: It is diagnosed in later life.
Family history is a factor, not direct inheritance.
It is typically silent until a fracture.

questions.prompt: Bone mineral density is assessed clinically using:
questions.why: DEXA measures calcified bone tissue, and the result correlates with bone strength.
distractorNotes: Blood calcium is defended and reveals little about bone.
Not the clinical standard.
Not sensitive enough for density.

questions.prompt: B vitamins matter to energy metabolism because they:
options: Act as coenzymes in the pathways
Are burned as fuel alongside glucose
Are stored and released when needed
Slow the rate of metabolism down
questions.why: They are functional parts of the machinery, not fuel for it. That is why a deficiency shows up as fatigue without the vitamin supplying any calories.
distractorNotes: Vitamins yield no energy at all.
Water-soluble vitamins are largely not stored.
They enable the pathways rather than slowing them.

questions.prompt: Minerals differ from the energy-yielding nutrients in that they:
options: Cannot be broken down for energy
Are needed in much larger amounts
Are absorbed only in the large bowel
Are made by the body when required
questions.why: A mineral is an element. There is nothing to break down. They act as cofactors for hundreds of enzymes instead.
distractorNotes: They are needed in small amounts.
Absorption is mainly in the small intestine.
Elements cannot be synthesised.

questions.prompt: Iron-deficiency anaemia reduces the blood's ability to:
questions.why: Too little iron means too little functional haemoglobin, and haemoglobin is what carries oxygen.
distractorNotes: Clotting involves platelets and clotting factors.
A different part of the immune system.
Not the primary function affected.

questions.prompt: The main cause of iron deficiency worldwide is:
options: Parasitic worm infection in the gut
Drinking too much water each day
questions.why: Blood loss from gut parasites is the leading cause globally — which makes it as much a public-health problem as a dietary one.
distractorNotes: Calcium can hinder absorption, but is not the main cause.
Not a cause of iron deficiency.
Cooking does not cause it.

questions.prompt: Someone taking a calcium supplement should also watch their:
questions.why: Calcium absorption depends on vitamin D. Without enough of it, the supplement delivers less than it appears to.
distractorNotes: Helps with iron, not calcium.
Affects absorption somewhat, but is not the pairing.
Relevant to bone, but not the pairing here.

checklist: List your calcium sources across one day and estimate the total.
Compare it with the recommendation for your age and sex.
Sort your own osteoporosis risk factors into modifiable and not.
Name one change you could make, and say which risk factor it addresses.
selfCheck: Did I check vitamin D alongside calcium?
Did I keep non-modifiable factors out of the action list?
applicationPrompts.aiPolicy: These are questions for you to answer. This app does not write any part of a submission.
